1#main: The law of a firstborn of a pure animal—at what time and in what place it applies. In it are 12 seifim. A firstborn of a pure animal applies to males and not to females; and it applies even when the Temple is not standing; both in Eretz Yisrael and in the Diaspora. And it is a mitzvah to sanctify it and say, "Behold this is holy," as it says, "you shall sanctify to the Lord your God"—and if he did not sanctify it, it is sanctified from the womb. (And they give it to the kohen and not to the kohenet (Tur).)
2#main: They do not give the firstborn to the kohen at birth, for this is not an honor for the kohen; rather the owner tends it until it grows somewhat. And how much must Israel tend it? For a small animal forty days, and for a large animal fifty days. And if he has no kohen available, he is obligated to tend it until a kohen becomes available to him.
3#main: If the kohen said to him, "Give it to me within this time and I will tend it myself," he is not permitted to give it to him—for this is like assisting with his gifts. And if he was blemished and said to him, "Within this time give it to me for I will eat it now," he is permitted to give it to him.
4#main: If the kohen refuses to receive it because there is great trouble at this time to tend it until a blemish falls in it, he is not permitted—because he appears to disparage priestly gifts. {Rama: And even a doubtful firstborn—the kohen must receive it immediately from the Israelite who gives it to him (Piskei Maharai siman 167 and Maharil siman 204). And specifically with a doubt that arose on its own; but in a place where the Israelite was negligent, such as one who bought a milking cow from a gentile, or who could have sold the firstborn to a gentile before it was born and did not do so—the kohen need not receive it (there). And even in a place where he must receive it, it is forbidden for an Israelite to give it to him to provoke him or to take revenge on him (likewise there in the name of Maharam).}
5#main: The firstborn at this time—they delay it until a blemish falls in it, and slaughter it according to an expert, and eat it everywhere; and one may feed it even to a gentile (or to dogs) (Hagahos Mordechai, chapter HaIshah SheHalachah).
6#main: The firstborn at this time—the kohen sells it, even to an Israelite, unblemished alive, and blemished alive, and slaughtered; and he betroths a woman with it as with his other property. But it is not sold by appraisal nor weighed by litra; nevertheless it is permitted to weigh it maneh against maneh, and against utensils and a kopitz (meaning: like a large broad knife whose sharpness protrudes in its middle)—and these matters apply to its flesh; but its milk, blood, forbidden fat, and horns are sold by appraisal and weighed by litra. And the fat of the forbidden sinew—its law is like flesh, since it is permitted by Torah.
7#main: The firstborn, even if blemished, is eaten within its year. From when is its year counted? If it was born blemished, its year is counted from the day it was born—provided he knows that its months are complete, for it is fit for eating on the day of its birth; but if he does not know with certainty that its months are complete, its year is counted from the day it is appraised.
8#main: If a blemish befell it within its year, he may maintain it all twelve months. If a blemish befell it at the end of its year, he may maintain it thirty days from the day the blemish befell it, even though it extends beyond its year. How so? For example, if a blemish befell it fifteen days before the completion of its year—they complete for it fifteen days after its year. If a blemish befell it after its year, he may not maintain it except thirty days and he eats it.
9#main: The firstborn at this time—until it is shown to a sage, one maintains it two or three years; and once it is shown to a sage, if a blemish befell it within its year he may maintain it all twelve months; and if a blemish befell it after its year, he maintains it thirty days.
10#main: The year of a firstborn is a complete lunar year—twelve months from day to day; and if the year was intercalated, it is intercalated for it and twelve months are counted for it.
11#main: If two lambs were born to him, one on the fifteenth of the first Adar and one on Rosh Chodesh of the second Adar—the one born on Rosh Chodesh of the second Adar, once the first day of Adar of the coming year arrives, a year has passed for it; and the one born in the middle of the first Adar—a year has not passed for it until the middle of Adar of the coming year, since it was born in the intercalary month—they count it for it.
12#main: If he transgressed and kept it beyond its time, it is not disqualified.
